title: Niche Vertical Scout & Procurement Trigger Catalog
creator: Sana Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Build a concise, operational catalog that maps emerging niche-vertical LLM entrants to procurement triggers (when they matter for customers) and to measurable signals (latency, token cost, availability, model provenance, fine-tuning/adapter support, and regulatory compatibility). This ticket focuses on research + an actionable signal-to-trigger crosswalk usable by Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Capacity Planning.

Scope:
- Identify 12 high-risk/high-opportunity niche verticals (e.g., legal contract summarization for EU firms, clinical triage assistants in APAC hospitals, regulatory-compliant RAG for fintech KYC) where model substitution or sudden availability changes materially affect buyer decisioning.
- For each vertical, capture: common workload profiles (avg context length, embedding vs. generation ratio), latency tolerance bands, cost sensitivity bands, and top-5 operational failure modes.
- Define procurement triggers: a concise set of signals (with thresholds) that should escalate to Procurement/Account Execs to consider Dedicated/Private options or to rotate fallback models.
- Deliver a dataset + simple classifier heuristics (rule-based) that converts telemetry and public signals into a 3-level urgency flag: Watch | Investigate | Escalate.

Deliverables: 
1) Catalog doc (Confluence/Drive) with vertical profiles and 1-page decision playbook per vertical.
2) Signal-to-trigger matrix CSV (columns: vertical, signal_name, metric_source, threshold, action).
3) Example monitoring queries (Datadog/Grafana/BigQuery) and a sample Dashboard wireframe.
4) Hand-off brief and 1-hour working session with Sales + Solutions (runbook + FAQ).

Success metrics:
- Catalog covers >=12 verticals with operationalized triggers.
- Playbook validated by at least 3 AE or Solutions interviews per vertical.
- The rule-based heuristics yield <=2 false-escalations per 1000 simulated signal windows on the synthetic workload lab.

Methodology / Data sources:
- Inbound telemetry: token volumes, 95th/99th pct latency by route, error budgets, model variant swaps.
- External signals: vendor status pages, GitHub release cadence, model-card change logs, public quantization notices.
- Field intelligence: AE interviews, support tickets, customer incident postmortems (anonymized).
- Synthetic workload lab: create 3 representative workloads per vertical to stress latency/cost/accuracy tradeoffs.

Stakeholders:
- Product (owner: Sana Kapoor)
- Solutions Eng (consult: Diego Marquez, Priya Nair)
- Sales leadership (consult: RVPs for FinServ / Health / Legal)
- Platform/Runtime (input on observability and sample queries)
- Research (help design synthetic workloads)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Overfitting triggers to current vendor behavior -> Mitigation: use conservative thresholds, require corroborating dual signals (e.g., latency spike + vendor outage RSS).
- Risk: Too many false positives -> Mitigation: run heuristics on historical telemetry and tune thresholds; expose opt-out toggles for low-touch customers.

Timeline & milestones:
- Week 1 (Mar 12–Mar 18): vertical selection, AE interview plan, initial telemetry sample queries.
- Week 2 (Mar 19–Mar 25): draft catalog pages + synthetic workload templates; run lab experiments for 4 verticals.
- Week 3 (Mar 26–Apr 1): finalize crosswalk CSV; QA heuristics against lab; design dashboard wireframe.
- Week 4 (Apr 2–Apr 8): stakeholder review, hand-off session, and PR/roadmap updates.

Open questions:
- Which telemetry retention window should we use to compute baseline percentiles for latency-sensitive triggers (30d vs 90d)? Proposal: start with 30d and expose 90d on request.
- Should procurement triggers be enforced automatically (auto-ticketing for CS/Procurement) or produce recommendations? Proposal: recommendation only for first 3 customers in pilot.

Next steps:
- Run quick scoped AE interviews (target 6 calls) this week; capture real customer anecdotes and sample SLOs.
- Pull 30d telemetry slice for candidate verticals and share synthetic workload template link.

Artifacts: https://drive.redwood.internal/scout-niche-verticals (draft), GH experiment harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scout-lab (lab harness), telemetry queries: https://grafana.redwood/project/telemetry-examples (wireframe).
